thread:
maya_support: FYI — we have an enterprise escalation from Planit (planit-inc). They say outputs got noticeably worse after last night's release. Multiple prompts that were previously fine are now hallucinating facts and changing tone. Customer attached sample.
maya_support: customer example: prompt -> "Summarize the security posture of AcmeCorp's SSO setup."
Response (before): "The SSO uses OIDC with Okta, enforces MFA, and rotates certs every 90 days."
Response (now): "AcmeCorp uses a proprietary token-based system with weekly rotation and no MFA (see logs)." — clearly incorrect.
maya_support: They said they didn't change their prompts. They're on hosted API (us-west). Want immediate rollback or mitigation. Escalation to account team started.
ben_product: :rotating_light: which release was pushed last night? Any deploy bot info?
deploy-bot: Deployed: service/inference-runtime v3.14.2 to prod-us-west @ 2026-03-04T03:12:45Z (deployer: diane_infra). Release notes: optimization + sampling-config refactor. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8569
cory_ml: Flagging likely culprit: PR 8569 touched the sampling defaults layer (moved default selection from model catalog to runtime). I left a comment in the PR but didn't realize default override was changed for hosted users.
diane_infra: I can roll back the deploy but want a safer targeted fix. Do we know whether customers omitted temperature/top_p and relied on old defaults? If yes, rollback to previous runtime default should restore prior behavior.
maya_support: Customer repro steps (copied from support ticket):
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"open-rl-1.0","input":"Summarize X","max_tokens":120}'
2) They don't pass temperature or top_p. Previously got stable concise summaries, now verbose/hallucinating.
emma_sre: Can you paste the exact curl + headers? Need to reproduce in a clean env. Also share model id and sample output from their logs.
maya_support: Provided (redacted):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_planit" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-rl-1.0","input":"Summarize the SSO setup for AcmeCorp","max_tokens":120}'
```
maya_support: Their recent response (trimmed): "...uses a proprietary token-based system...no MFA...weekly rotation..."
cory_ml: I pulled the runtime config history. Previous runtime defaults: temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, typical_p=.95. After the refactor, default values in runtime config are temp=0.6, top_p=1.0. That would absolutely push more creativity and hallucination.
cory_ml: The PR was intended to centralize defaults but the intended per-model overrides in the model catalog weren't applied. It's a bug.
ben_product: Noted. Two-step plan: (1) short-term revert the sampling-default changes in prod (rollback or config flip), (2) add an explicit migration test + add telemetry to detect sudden distribution shifts in outputs whenever defaults change.
diane_infra: I can flip the feature flag to force the old defaults for hosted traffic in us-west. On it if you approve. That avoids full rollback.
ben_product: Approve. Do it and post the flag flip command/log here. Also assign a rollback/PR to patch the runtime to respect model-catalog overrides.
diane_infra: Flipped feature flag sampling_defaults_v2 -> false for prod-us-west. Command: `infractl feature toggle sampling_defaults_v2 --env prod-us-west --off`
Action log:
```
2026-03-04T04:05:12Z - infractl - user:diane_infra - toggled sampling_defaults_v2=false - target: prod-us-west
2026-03-04T04:05:13Z - infractl - rollout 3/3 nodes updated
2026-03-04T04:05:28Z - infractl - verification: smoke-checks passed (generate success rate 99.8%)
```
deploy-bot: Feature flag change recorded in audit log: https://audit.redwood.local/flags/xyz
emma_sre: I ran a quick AB check against a cached prompt set (n=120) comparing responses before and after the flag flip — the distribution of hallucination markers dropped from 18% -> 3% (quick heuristic). Looks promising but need longer run.
maya_support: Customer confirmed initial sample looks closer to previous output after ~15 minutes. They're asking for timeline and root cause explanation.
cory_ml: Root cause: the runtime refactor introduced new global defaults (higher temperature/top_p). Because many customers do not send sampling params, they effectively got the new aggressive defaults. Fix: patch runtime to (a) default to model-catalog's specified sampling-profile when present, (b) keep prior global default if not overridden. Also update SDKs/docs to encourage explicit sampling params.
ben_product: I'll draft a postmortem/blame-free incident note and coordinate comms with account team. Also add an opt-in canary for future default changes and an automatic alert if downstream output quality metrics shift >5% within 1 hour.
maya_support: Tickets: PLANIT-934 (customer), SUPPORT-4201 (general). I've updated customer to expect a technical write-up and ETA for a permanent fix (ETA end of week). They're ok with the flag flip for now.
diane_infra: Creating a hotfix PR to ensure runtime respects model-catalog overrides and keeps legacy default otherwise: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8612 — assigning to cory_ml for review.
cory_ml: Reviewing now. Also adding regression tests that simulate users omitting sampling params.
ben_product: Action items:
- cory_ml: merge hotfix + tests (ETA 24h)
- diane_infra: coordinate canary rollout after merge (ETA next morning)
- maya_support: send templated customer note + follow-up once hotfix is in
- emma_sre: schedule 12h re-run of hallucination detection job on production prompts (monitor)
maya_support: Thanks team. Planit remains on hold for now but not canceling. I'll keep thread updated with customer responses. :thumbsup:
emma_sre: Adding monitoring alert: REDWOOD-ALERT-713 created. If hallucination heuristic > 7% we page.
maya_support: Closing loop in support ticket with links to this thread and feature-flag audit. Will reopen if customer sees more anomalies.

ben_product: Good catch. Let's also add a small docs blurb underneath "sampling" that says: "If you do not provide sampling params, the system will apply model-specific defaults. If no model-specific defaults exist, a conservative global default is used." — to prevent surprises.
maya_support: Will include that in the customer note. Closing here for now.
